faq.q: What is the difference between an audit, a review and a compilation?
faq.a: A compilation means the accountant prepares the annual financial statements from your records without expressing an assurance opinion. An independent review and an audit are assurance engagements with progressively more testing. Which one your company needs depends on its Public Interest Score and its Memorandum of Incorporation. Most owner-managed small companies in South Africa require only a compilation.

faq.q: How often should bookkeeping be done?
faq.a: Monthly, in almost every case. Monthly bookkeeping keeps VAT returns accurate, makes payroll reconciliations straightforward, and means year-end is a review rather than a scramble. It also means you can see how the business is actually performing while you can still do something about it.

faq.q: Do you work with Xero, Sage, QuickBooks or spreadsheets?

faq.q: My books are years behind. Is that a problem?

title: Tax Services & SARS Returns Gqeberha | Knoesen Accounting
description: Income tax, provisional tax and VAT returns for individuals and companies in Gqeberha, plus SARS registrations, disputes and overdue return clean-ups.
lead: Returns filed correctly and on time, and a straight answer when SARS sends something you do not understand.

faq.q: Am I a provisional taxpayer?
faq.a: Generally, you are a provisional taxpayer if you earn income that is not subject to PAYE — such as business income, rental income or significant investment income. Someone who earns only a salary usually is not. There is an exemption where income from interest, dividends, foreign dividends, rental from fixed property and remuneration from an unregistered employer totals R30 000 or less for the tax year.

faq.q: What happens if I file my tax return late?
faq.a: SARS charges administrative non-compliance penalties that recur every month a return remains outstanding, and interest accrues on any unpaid tax. The penalties are levied per outstanding return, so several late years compound quickly. Filing late is always better than not filing.

faq.q: Can you deal with SARS on my behalf?
faq.a: Yes. Once you appoint us and we are linked to your profile on SARS eFiling, we can submit returns, respond to verification requests, and handle correspondence directly with SARS on your behalf.

faq.q: I received an auto-assessment. Do I need to do anything?
faq.a: Only if it is wrong or incomplete. An auto-assessment uses third-party data SARS already holds. If you have deductions SARS does not know about — home office costs, travel claims, retirement annuity contributions or medical expenses not on a scheme certificate — you should file a return rather than accept it.

title: Payroll Services Gqeberha | PAYE, UIF & SDL Compliance
description: Outsourced payroll in Gqeberha: payslips, EMP201 and EMP501 submissions, IRP5 certificates, UIF and SDL. For teams of one to a hundred.
lead: Staff paid correctly, PAYE and UIF submitted on time, and IRP5s that reconcile at year-end without drama.

faq.q: When must PAYE, UIF and SDL be paid over to SARS?
faq.a: The EMP201 declaration and payment are due within seven days after the end of the month the deductions relate to. Where the seventh falls on a weekend or public holiday, the deadline moves to the last business day before it.

faq.q: Does my business have to pay the Skills Development Levy?
faq.a: SDL is levied at 1% of total remuneration paid to employees. Employers whose total annual remuneration is less than R500 000 are exempt from paying SDL.

faq.q: How much UIF must be contributed?
faq.a: Unemployment insurance contributions are payable monthly, made up of 1% contributed by the employer and 1% by the employee, based on the employee's remuneration below a prescribed ceiling.

faq.q: When are the EMP501 reconciliations due?
faq.a: There are two each year: an interim reconciliation covering March to August, and an annual reconciliation covering the full tax year. These are what generate employees' IRP5 and IT3(a) certificates, so errors here surface directly on your staff's tax returns.

faq.q: What happens if I do not file my CIPC annual return?
faq.a: CIPC may place the company in deregistration process and ultimately deregister it. A deregistered company loses its legal existence: its bank accounts can be frozen, it cannot contract lawfully, and directors lose the protection of separate legal personality. Reinstatement is possible but slower and more expensive than simply filing on time.

faq.q: When is my CIPC annual return due?
faq.a: Companies must file within 30 business days after the anniversary of their date of incorporation. Close corporations file within the anniversary month of incorporation and the two months following. The fee is based on turnover, and it is separate from your SARS income tax return — the two are often confused.

faq.q: What is a beneficial ownership declaration?
faq.a: South African companies and close corporations must file information about the natural persons who ultimately own or effectively control the entity. It is filed with CIPC alongside the annual return, and non-compliance can block the annual return from being accepted.

faq.q: Can you register a new company for me?
faq.a: Yes — company registration at CIPC, income tax registration at SARS, and UIF registration at the Department of Employment and Labour. See our checklist for what is involved.

faq.q: When does Filing Season 2026 close?
faq.a: Non-provisional individual taxpayers have until 23 October 2026. Provisional taxpayers and trusts have until 22 January 2027.

faq.q: What is an auto-assessment?
faq.a: SARS issues an auto-assessment using third-party data it already holds from employers, banks, medical schemes and retirement funds. Auto-assessment notices for 2026 were issued from 1 to 12 July 2026. If the assessment is correct and complete, no further action is needed.

faq.q: Should I accept my auto-assessment?
faq.a: Only if it captures everything. SARS does not know about deductions it has no third-party record of, such as home office expenses, business travel against a travel allowance, or out-of-pocket medical costs. If any of those apply, file a return rather than accepting the auto-assessment.

title: VAT Registration Threshold South Africa: Now R2.3 Million
description: From 1 April 2026 the compulsory VAT registration threshold rose from R1 million to R2.3 million. What changed, who it affects, and whether to deregister.
h1: The VAT registration threshold is now R2.3 million
lead: On 1 April 2026 the compulsory VAT registration threshold more than doubled. If your turnover sits between R1 million and R2.3 million, this directly affects you.

faq.q: What is the VAT registration threshold in South Africa?
faq.a: A vendor that makes taxable supplies of more than R2.3 million per annum must register for VAT. This threshold increased from R1 million with effect from 1 April 2026.

faq.q: Can I register for VAT voluntarily?
faq.a: Yes. A business making taxable supplies of more than R120 000 but not more than R2.3 million per annum may apply for voluntary VAT registration.

faq.q: Is the South African VAT rate still 15%?
faq.a: Yes. VAT is levied at the standard rate of 15% on the supply of goods and services by registered vendors. The increases proposed in 2025 were reversed and the rate was left unchanged in Budget 2026.

faq.q: Should I deregister for VAT now that the threshold has increased?
faq.a: It depends on who your customers are. If you sell mainly to other VAT-registered businesses, they reclaim the VAT you charge, and staying registered lets you keep claiming input VAT on your own costs. If you sell mainly to consumers, deregistering can make you effectively cheaper. There are also exit consequences, including output VAT on assets held at deregistration, so it is worth modelling before deciding.

title: Small Business Tax South Africa 2026/27 | SBC vs Turnover Tax
description: How South African small businesses are taxed in 2026/27: 27% company tax, Small Business Corporation rates from 0%, and turnover tax under R2.3 million.
h1: How small businesses are taxed in South Africa
lead: There are three different ways a small South African business can be taxed, and the gap between them is worth real money. Here is how to tell which one applies to you.

faq.q: What is the company tax rate in South Africa?
faq.a: The standard corporate income tax rate is 27% of taxable income, applying to years of assessment ending on any date from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027.

faq.q: What is a Small Business Corporation?
faq.a: A Small Business Corporation is a company, close corporation or co-operative that meets specific requirements in section 12E of the Income Tax Act, including a gross income limit, shareholders who are natural persons holding no other company shares, and a limit on income from personal or professional services. Qualifying entities are taxed on a graduated scale starting at 0% rather than a flat 27%.

faq.q: Who qualifies for turnover tax?
faq.a: Micro businesses with a qualifying annual turnover of R2.3 million or less may elect turnover tax. It replaces income tax, VAT, provisional tax, capital gains tax and dividends tax with a single simplified calculation on turnover rather than profit.

faq.q: Is turnover tax always cheaper?
faq.a: No. Turnover tax is calculated on turnover, not profit, so a business with thin margins or a loss-making year can pay turnover tax while owing no income tax at all. It suits high-margin, low-cost businesses with simple affairs. It is a calculation worth doing rather than a rule of thumb.

title: Independent Contractor or Employee? The SARS Tests | South Africa
description: SARS's tests for contractor vs employee: the three-employee rule, the dominant impression test, and why unpaid PAYE lands on the employer.
h1: Independent contractor or employee? What SARS actually tests
lead: A signed contract calling someone a contractor decides nothing. These are the tests SARS applies — and the PAYE risk sits with you, not them.

faq.q: Who is liable if SARS decides my contractor was really an employee?
faq.a: The employer. SARS Interpretation Note 17 places the duty to determine whether payments are subject to employees' tax on the employer, because the employer is best placed to evaluate the actual working relationship. If PAYE should have been withheld and was not, the employer becomes liable for that tax plus penalties and interest, regardless of what the contract says or that the worker invoiced you.

faq.q: Does employing three people make me an independent contractor?
faq.a: Yes, for PAYE purposes. A person who employs three or more full-time employees who are not connected persons, and who are engaged in the business throughout the year of assessment, is deemed to be carrying on a trade independently. This is the overriding statutory test: it takes precedence over the other statutory test and over the common-law position. Family members and connected trusts do not count.

faq.q: Can I get a letter from SARS confirming someone is an independent contractor?
faq.a: No. SARS branch offices previously issued “Letters of Independence”, but that practice has stopped and the ability to reject such applications is now codified in the Tax Administration Act. You must make and document the determination yourself.

faq.q: What is the dominant impression test?
faq.a: Where neither statutory test settles the question, SARS weighs about 20 indicators of the working relationship, grouped as near-conclusive (control of manner, payment regime, who must render the service, client base, risk and profit), persuasive (supervision, reports, training, control of hours) and resonant (whose tools and premises, integration into the business). No single indicator decides it, and SARS is explicit that the grid is a guide rather than a scorecard.

faq.q: Do I have to withhold PAYE when paying a labour broker?
faq.a: Yes, unless the labour broker holds a valid IRP30 exemption certificate. SARS treats this as an anti-avoidance measure that must be applied strictly, so ask for the certificate before paying rather than after.

title: SARS Income Tax & PAYE Calculator 2026/27 & 2025/26 | SA
description: Free South African income tax calculator for 2026/27 and 2025/26. Work out monthly PAYE and take-home pay, with age rebates, medical credits and retirement contributions.
lead: Enter what you earn and see your PAYE, your take-home pay, and exactly how the figure was reached — bracket by bracket.

faq.q: How much tax do I pay on my salary in South Africa in 2026/27?
faq.a: It depends on your taxable income and your age. The first R99 000 a year is effectively tax free for someone under 65, because the R17 820 primary rebate cancels the tax on it. Above that, income is taxed in bands from 18% up to 45% on income over R1 878 600. Only the portion of income inside each band is taxed at that band's rate, so moving into a higher bracket never reduces your take-home pay.

faq.q: What is the tax threshold for 2026/27?
faq.a: R99 000 a year if you are under 65, R153 250 if you are 65 to 74, and R171 300 if you are 75 or older. Below the threshold for your age no income tax is payable, though you may still need to submit a return.

faq.q: How is PAYE different from income tax?
faq.a: PAYE is not a separate tax. It is your income tax collected in monthly instalments by your employer and paid over to SARS on your behalf. At the end of the tax year SARS compares the PAYE withheld against the tax actually due on your assessment, which is why you can end up with a refund or a shortfall.

faq.q: How much of my retirement annuity is tax deductible?
faq.a: Contributions to pension, provident and retirement annuity funds are deductible up to 27.5% of the greater of your remuneration or your taxable income, capped at R430 000 a year. Anything above the limit is not lost — it carries forward to the next tax year.

faq.q: Is this calculator accurate for my situation?
faq.a: It is accurate for a salaried employee on steady pay, and uses the official Budget 2026 rates. It does not account for a travel allowance or company car, the additional medical expenses tax credit, commission or freelance income, lump sums, or capital gains. If any of those apply, treat the result as a starting point and speak to an accountant.

title: VAT Calculator South Africa 2026 | Add or Remove 15% VAT
description: Free South African VAT calculator. Add 15% VAT to a price, or work out the VAT inside a VAT-inclusive amount using the 15/115 fraction.
lead: Add VAT to a price, or take it back out of one. The second is where most VAT returns go wrong.

faq.q: How do I calculate 15% VAT in South Africa?
faq.a: To add VAT to a price that excludes it, multiply by 1.15. To find the VAT inside a VAT-inclusive amount, multiply by 15 and divide by 115. On R1 150 including VAT, the VAT is R150 and the VAT-exclusive value is R1 000.

faq.q: How do I remove VAT from a total?
faq.a: Divide the VAT-inclusive amount by 1.15, or equivalently multiply it by 15/115. Do not simply take 15% off the inclusive amount — that is the most common VAT error and it understates the VAT every time.

faq.q: When must I register for VAT in South Africa?
faq.a: Registration is compulsory once your taxable supplies exceed R2.3 million in any twelve consecutive months. You may register voluntarily once taxable supplies exceed R120 000. The compulsory threshold rose from R1 million in Budget 2026.

faq.q: What is the VAT rate in South Africa?
faq.a: The standard rate is 15%. Certain supplies are zero-rated (such as most basic foodstuffs and exports) or exempt (such as residential rent and most financial services).
